new_scholarship.description: The Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI) offers annual government scholarships to foreign students and to Italian citizens living abroad (IRE) for onsite study, training or research at Italian state or legally recognised private institutions, under Italian law 288/55 and its subsequent amendments and additions. For the 2026-2027 academic year the award pays a fixed EUR 10,800 over a non-deferable nine-month period from 1 November 2026 to 31 July 2027, disbursed in three instalments of EUR 5,500, EUR 2,300 and EUR 3,000 into a personal Italian bank account, alongside collective health insurance contracted by MAECI. Selection is made by citizenship from a published list of eligible countries and other territories, applications are submitted exclusively through the MAECI Study in Italy portal, and each application is examined by a committee of the competent Italian diplomatic representation, with an interview for those who pass the comparative evaluation. For new applicants in the 2026-2027 Call a full bachelor's degree is funded only through the AFAM first-cycle route in paragraph 1.2; the general Laurea triennale (1st cycle) category in paragraph 1.6, the "Costruiamo il futuro" scholarships, is reserved exclusively for renewals of students who already benefited from that scholarship in 2025-2026.
new_scholarship.best_fit: A secondary-school graduate (or final-year upper-secondary student) from one of the 157 eligible countries and territories, or an IRE applicant holding sole Italian citizenship and resident in one of the 20 named IRE countries, who wants to enrol in the first year of an Italian AFAM first-cycle programme in fine arts, music or dance, is 18-28 years old at the Call deadline, can evidence CEFR B2 in the language of instruction of the chosen programme, has not studied or graduated in Italy, and can self-fund tuition, regional taxes, travel, accommodation and living costs. Also a fit for a current "Costruiamo il futuro" or other MAECI scholarship holder applying for a renewal of the same programme at the same institution under Article 3.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Selection is made strictly by citizenship, from the list of eligible foreign countries and other territories published for the academic year (157 entries for 2026-2027, including the United Kingdom, Germany, France, Spain, Canada, Australia, Brazil, China, India, Japan, Turkey and Singapore but excluding, for example, the United States, the Netherlands, Ireland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland and New Zealand); an applicant may compete for one country only. Applicants must hold a valid passport or identity document and must not be enrolled in, or have graduated from, an Italian or foreign secondary school in Italy, an Italian higher-education institution (university or AFAM) in Italy, or a foreign higher-education institution located in Italy, and must not enrol in any year other than the first year of the chosen programme. For the Laurea triennale / AFAM 1st-cycle route the applicant must hold the academic qualification required for enrolment by the chosen institution; applicants must be of age and not exceed 28 years at the Call deadline (born on or after 27 March 1997), with renewals the sole exception. Language competence of at least CEFR B2 in the language of instruction is required (Italian B2 for Italian-taught programmes, English B2 for English-taught programmes). Applicants must not have carried out MAECI-funded research projects in the last five academic years (2021-2022 to 2025-2026 inclusive), must not be employees of the Italian Public Administration or their first-degree descendants, and must not be enrolled part-time or beyond the legal duration of the programme. For the 2026-2027 Call the ordinary bachelor's (Laurea triennale, 1st cycle) category is closed to new applicants: it is funded only through paragraph 1.6 "Costruiamo il futuro", which is reserved for renewals of prior-year holders.

new_scholarship.english_requirement: CEFR level B2 in English for English-taught programmes under paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2. The Call does not name a specific test and publishes no minimum IELTS, TOEFL, PTE or Duolingo score and no validity period. Applicants who have completed an entirely English-taught Bachelor's degree may instead upload a document stating that the study programme was entirely held in English, and applicants from countries where English is an official language may upload a self-declaration of at least B2 proficiency. No proof of Italian language proficiency is required for programmes entirely taught in English.
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Applications are examined by a committee established by the Italian diplomatic representation competent for the applicant's territory. Awarding follows six published stages: (1) comparative evaluation of the applications received through the Study in Italy portal on the requirements and on criteria relating to the merit of the applicant's educational background, to decide admission to the interview; (2) an interview with only those candidates who passed the comparative evaluation; (3) publication of the merit ranking; (4) any required uploading of supplementary documents; (5) acceptance or refusal of the scholarship by the candidate; (6) receipt, acknowledgement and acceptance of the awarding letter. The ranking is published on the website of the competent diplomatic representation and is unappealable; only winners are notified through the portal. No numeric weighting of academic merit against interview performance is published. For the 'Costruiamo il futuro' category in the 2025-2026 Call, priority was given to applicants enrolling in engineering, computer science, economics, agriculture or medical-health programmes, in line with the priorities of Piano Mattei.

new_scholarship.notes:
BACHELOR'S-LEVEL FINDING (the most important caveat on this record): for the 2026-2027 academic year the Call funds a full bachelor's degree for NEW applicants only through the AFAM route in paragraph 1.2, 'Higher Education for Fine Arts, Music and Dance (AFAM) programmes (1st and 2nd cycle)'. Paragraph 2.4.2 states in full that MAECI scholarships are 'neither available nor granted' for attending: 'Bachelor's Degree programmes (1st cycle or "Lauree triennali"), except for AFAM programmes and without prejudice to the provisions set out in article 1.6'. Paragraph 1.6, the 'Costruiamo il futuro' scholarships for Bachelor's Degree (Laurea Triennale, 1st cycle) or Single-Cycle Degree programmes, states that 'This type of scholarship is reserved exclusively for the purposes of renewal to students who benefited from the "Costruiamo il futuro" scholarship according to articles 1.6 and 7 of the Call for applications for the academic year 2025-2026'. The record therefore documents a bachelor-capable award whose open route for new applicants is AFAM 1st cycle, plus the renewal route for Laurea triennale via 'Costruiamo il futuro'.

COSTRUIAMO IL FUTURO: in the 2025-2026 Call (which is the scheme that produced the renewals funded in 2026-2027) Article 7 offered a reserve of twelve 9-month grants 'In order to connect students from Italian schools in Africa to the Italian university education system' to students attending the final year of upper secondary school in 2024-2025 at four named Italian schools: Istituto Italiano Omnicomprensivo 'G. Galilei' in Addis Ababa (3 grants), Scuole Italiane Paritarie 'E. Mattei' in Casablanca (3), Istituto Salesiano 'Don Bosco' in Cairo (3) and Istituto Scolastico Italiano 'G.B. Hodierna' in Tunis (3). Those grants funded enrolment in Bachelor's Degree (Laurea triennale) or Single-Cycle Degree programmes, with priority to engineering, computer science, economics, agriculture or medical-health programmes in line with Piano Mattei, and applicants had to be of age and not exceed 23 at the 2025-2026 deadline. The 2025-2026 total was EUR 9,000 in three instalments of EUR 4,500, EUR 2,500 and EUR 2,000; the 2026-2027 renewal amount is EUR 10,800.

FUNDING: EUR 10,800 is the total published in Article 11 of the Call for paragraphs 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4 and 1.6, paid in three instalments. No monthly rate is published, so funding_amount is the published lump-sum total rather than a derived monthly figure. The full amount requires the recipient to be present in Italy by 15 November 2026; recipients arriving on or after 16 November 2026 have the scholarship reduced proportionally by arrival date, with renewals excepted. Paragraph 1.5 (Italofonia language courses) pays a separate EUR 3,600 in one instalment over 3 months and is a non-degree short course, so it is not the amount used here.

TUITION: not covered. Article 9 states that some universities exempt scholarship recipients from enrolment and tuition fees under the university-autonomy rules of Italian Legislative Decree 68 of 29 March 2012, but recipients must ask the chosen institution, and the fees are not refundable by MAECI. Regional taxes are due in any case, are borne by the student and are not refundable by MAECI. The exemption does not apply to intensive Italian language and culture courses. 'fully_funded' must therefore be false even though the stipend is substantial.

AGE: the Call's age ceiling for the categories that include the bachelor-level route is 28 years at the deadline (born on or after 27 March 1997) with renewals the sole exception. Renewals excepted means a candidate who is already a scholarship holder is not bound by this ceiling, which is why the same sentence in the Italian and English texts ends 'con l'eccezione dei soli rinnovi'.

OTHER: The award is incompatible with any other scholarship from the Italian Government or any other Italian public institution, including regional right-to-education scholarships; it is compatible with internships abroad, Erasmus and Erasmus+ and other internationally funded programmes, but is not paid during periods of study, research or internship outside Italy. Absence from Italy exceeding 15 consecutive days must be notified with justification and may be granted only once per funding period, with a limited exception around the Christmas teaching break. Payment is made only to a personal current account with an Italian bank, after verification of the date of entry into Italy, certification of enrolment by the institution named in the awarding letter, and submission of the Italian tax identification number and IBAN. Employees of the Italian Public Administration and their first-degree descendants are excluded. Article 5 reserves three 9-month 'Attanasio' scholarships for applicants from Morocco, Nigeria and the Democratic Republic of Congo in international relations, development cooperation, international humanitarian and human-rights law, with a preference for the named LM classes; that reserve is master's-level and is not a bachelor's route. The Call publishes no total number of scholarships offered for 2026-2027 and no per-country allocation, so the intensity of competition in any single country cannot be stated from the official source.

CYCLE DATES: the 2025-2026 Call closed at 14:00 Italian time on 16 May 2025 and the 2026-2027 Call closed at 14:00 Italian time on 26 March 2026, so the deadline has not yet settled into a fixed month. The Study in Italy portal page for the current call still carries the stale wording that 'The call for applications for MAECI grants for the 2025-2026 academic year is now closed'; the substantive closure note for the 2026-2027 cycle is on the MAECI page and in the Call itself. No date has been published for the 2027-2028 Call, so status_note carries the next-cycle expectation as an expectation only.

programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: Selection is strictly by citizenship, from the list of eligible foreign countries and other territories published for the academic year (157 entries for 2026-2027); an applicant may compete for one country only. Applicants must not hold a secondary-school or higher-education qualification obtained in Italy and must not be enrolled in any such institution located in Italy, so study previously pursued in Italy disqualifies.

programme_detail_official.description: The Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation offers scholarships in favour of foreign students and Italian citizens living abroad (IRE) for the 2026-2027 academic year, in order to foster cooperation in the cultural, scientific and technological fields, to support Italy's economic system in the world and to promote the Italian language and culture, according to Italian law 288/55 and its subsequent amendments and additions. Scholarships are offered for study, training or research programmes at public or legally recognised private Italian institutions and are awarded exclusively for the onsite attendance of academic courses on Italian territory. Selection is by citizenship from the published list of eligible countries and other territories, and applications are accepted only through the Study in Italy portal. For the 2026-2027 Call the categories are: Laurea magistrale 2nd cycle (1.1); AFAM fine arts, music and dance at 1st and 2nd cycle (1.2); PhD programmes (1.3); research projects (1.4); Italofonia intensive Italian language and culture courses (1.5); and Bachelor's Degree or single-cycle degree scholarships under the 'Costruiamo il futuro' name (1.6), which is reserved exclusively for renewals.
programme_detail_official.coverage: EUR 10,800 lump sum for the fixed 9-month award period, of which EUR 5,500 is earmarked for arrival and settling-in in Italy, paid in three instalments into a personal Italian bank account, plus MAECI-contracted collective health insurance for illness and accident for the duration of the scholarship. Tuition, regional taxes, travel to Italy, accommodation, study materials and living costs beyond the instalments are not covered; some universities may exempt recipients from enrolment and tuition fees under Legislative Decree 68/2012 but this is institution-specific and must be verified case by case.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your citizenship appears on the eligible-countries list for the cycle you want to apply to, before doing anything else: the list is re-published every academic year and it changes between cycles.

If you hold Italian citizenship plus another, know which route you are taking: dual Italian and foreign citizens compete only through the foreign beneficiary country selection, so the field to fill in on the portal is your foreign citizenship.
Check the age ceiling against your date of birth. The ceiling is counted at the Call deadline, not at submission of later documents, so compute your age on the deadline date.

Decide early whether your target is an AFAM first-cycle programme or, if you already hold a MAECI scholarship, a renewal. New applicants to an ordinary Laurea triennale are not eligible in the 2026-2027 cycle.

Ask the AFAM institution for its own admission requirements in writing. The Call explicitly says that admission tests and pre-enrolment procedures are set by the institution, and the MAECI award follows the institution's decision, not the reverse.
Book the language test early enough that the certificate is in hand at application, or at least in time to upload it during the supplementary-document window if your category permits it.
Get your passport renewed now if it expires within the next 18 months. A copy is uploaded at registration and a valid passport is required at the visa stage.
Set aside the money for tuition and regional taxes before you apply. Nothing in the award covers them, and the regional tax is due regardless of any institutional exemption.
Register on the Study in Italy portal well before the deadline and submit early. The Call warns that portal slowdowns from high traffic are not accepted as an excuse for a late submission.
Use an email address you check daily for the portal registration, because award stages, requests for supplementary documents and results all arrive there.
Prepare a plain-language explanation of how you will fund the parts MAECI does not pay. There is no published financial-need test at the MAECI stage, but you still need the money to be in Italy.
common_rejection_risks: Believing that MAECI funds any Italian bachelor's degree. For the 2026-2027 cycle it does not: the ordinary Laurea triennale is excluded except for AFAM programmes and 'Costruiamo il futuro' renewals, so a general undergraduate applicant has no open route.
Applying for a Laurea magistrale a ciclo unico (single-cycle degree) or a university Master, a specialisation course or a single course, all of which are explicitly not funded.
Your citizenship not being on the list for the cycle you apply in, or having been on a previous list but removed since.
Having studied or graduated in Italy. Holding an Italian secondary-school diploma or a degree from any Italian or foreign institution located in Italy disqualifies you outright.
Trying to enrol in the second or third year rather than the first year of the programme.

Missing the supplementary-document window because you assumed you could upload a pending qualification or language certificate at any time. For paragraphs 1.4, 1.5, 1.6 and renewals, nothing can be added after submission at all.
Uploading a pre-admission letter for a PhD place instead of the definitive admission letter; pre-admission letters are not accepted in any circumstance.
Waiting until the last days to submit, then blaming portal traffic.
Missing the interview because you did not monitor the email address registered on the portal.
Not being in Italy by 15 November 2026 and therefore receiving a proportionally reduced scholarship, or not having the Italian tax identification number and IBAN in time to be paid at all.
Holding another Italian Government or Italian public scholarship, including a regional right-to-education scholarship, which makes you incompatible with this award.
Being an employee of the Italian Public Administration, or a first-degree descendant of one.
Absence from Italy of more than 15 consecutive days without notifying MAECI, which risks a reduction you can only contest once.
Assuming a visa is guaranteed: you must apply for the visa and tax identification number before the start date and obtain them in time.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees and university contributions at the chosen AFAM institution, unless that institution exempts you under its university-autonomy powers. Ask for the exemption in writing before you enrol.
Regional taxes, which the Call states are always due, are borne by the student and are never refunded by MAECI.
Living costs beyond the EUR 10,800 for the 9-month period: the instalments are fixed and the first is meant for arrival and settling-in, so nothing extra arrives if you overspend early.
Travel to Italy and back: no travel allowance or reimbursement exists.
Accommodation deposit and first months' rent, plus furniture, utilities and local transport.
Health costs outside the MAECI collective policy, which excludes conditions dependent on pre-existing physical or pathological states and all dental care.
Costs of transitional or preparatory courses before the enrolled programme, which the Call states are not covered by scholarship payments.
Application or enrolment fees at the institution, and any fee the institution charges for its own admission tests.
Language-test fees, document translations, legalisation, recognition procedures, passport, visa and residence-permit costs.
document_audit: Scan your passport now and check the copy is genuinely legible on screen: the Call makes an unreadable copy a ground for exclusion.
If you hold Italian citizenship, find your passport, Italian ID card or a valid citizenship certificate and upload the proof.
Confirm which of your papers is the qualification valid for enrolment at the specific AFAM programme you have chosen; a generic certificate sometimes is not.
Check the date of any language certificate you already hold. The Call publishes no validity period, but institutions often impose their own, so ask.
If you are relying on an English-taught degree instead of a test, get a signed statement from your university confirming the programme was entirely taught in English.
If you are an English self-declaration case (official-language country), prepare the self-declaration format your diplomiatic representation accepts and confirm it early.
For renewals, download the updated certificate or self-declaration from your university website, sign it by hand, and check that the credit count matches what the portal asks for.
Keep one clean PDF per document with a filename that makes the document obvious; the portal upload process is unforgiving of confused filenames.
Have translations and any legalisation ready before you start, because the portal does not wait for them.
After submitting, save the confirmation and note the date: absence of a valid upload is treated as if nothing was sent.

alerts.message: Do not submit on the deadline day. The Call states that portal slowdowns from high traffic are not accepted as valid grounds for failure to submit, so submit days in advance.

If you want a general Laurea triennale as a new applicant, this cycle has no open category for you: MAECI scholarships are not granted for 1st-cycle degrees except AFAM programmes and 'Costruiamo il futuro' renewals. Look at an Italian university scholarship instead.

The 2026-2027 Call closed at 14:00 Italian time on 26 March 2026. You cannot apply to that cycle. Watch the Study in Italy call list page for the next cycle rather than any date you may find quoted elsewhere.

The MAECI award does not replace your admission. Pre-enrolment, admission tests and enrolment are separate and are decided by the AFAM institution; without a valid enrolment certificate the scholarship cannot be disbursed.

Your arrival date determines how much of the scholarship you actually receive. Being in Italy by 15 November 2026 preserves the full amount; arriving on or after 16 November 2026 costs you a proportional cut.

If you already hold a 'Costruiamo il futuro' or other MAECI scholarship, you must renew the same programme at the same institution, you cannot exceed the legal duration, and no documents may be added after submission for renewals.
Do not assume tuition is covered. Ask the institution in writing about the exemption and about regional taxes; both can fall on you, and neither is refundable by MAECI.

submission_workflow: Verify that your citizenship is on the current eligible-countries list for the academic year you intend to start.
Identify the exact programme and category you will apply under (AFAM 1st cycle via 1.2, renewal via 3 / 1.6, etc.) and confirm the specific documents that category allows.
Register on the Study in Italy portal with an email address you check daily and upload a legible passport or identity document copy.
Declare any Italian citizenship and upload the proof.
Complete the online application selecting the single beneficiary country corresponding to your citizenship.
Upload the academic qualification valid for enrolment, or declare that it is not yet held if your category permits a later upload.
Upload the language proficiency certificate required for your programme, or declare it as pending where permitted.
For research projects and for some renewal types, attach the tutor invitation letter, research project or supervisory evaluation letter at the time of application.
Submit the application well before the 14:00 Italian deadline and keep the confirmation.
Monitor the registered email for requests to upload supplementary documents, and upload them by the published supplementary-document deadline if your category qualifies.
Prepare for and attend the interview if called; only candidates who pass the comparative evaluation are interviewed.
Check the winners and reserve ranking published by the competent Italian diplomatic representation, and accept or decline the scholarship if offered.
Read and accept the Dichiarazione di assegnazione di borsa di studio (awarding letter) sent by the diplomatic representation.
Complete pre-enrolment or enrolment at the chosen institution, and apply for the Italian tax identification number and the study visa in time for the 1 November start.
Provide the Italian tax identification number and IBAN, and be present in Italy by 15 November 2026 to receive the full amount.
For renewals only: re-apply through the ordinary portal procedure for the same programme at the same institution with the credit certificate.

Paragraph 1.6 reads 'Corsi di Laurea triennale (1° ciclo) e Laurea magistrale a ciclo unico: borse di studio Costruiamo il futuro', and states that 'This type of scholarship is reserved exclusively for the purposes of renewal to students who benefited from the Costruiamo il futuro scholarship according to articles 1.6 and 7 of the Call for applications for the academic year 2025-2026'. Paragraph 2.4.2 confirms the boundary: MAECI scholarships are 'neither available nor granted' for 'Bachelor's Degree programmes (1st cycle or Lauree triennali), except for AFAM programmes and without prejudice to the provisions set out in article 1.6', and not for single-cycle degree programmes. The bachelor's-level coverage is therefore: AFAM 1st cycle open to new applicants, plus Laurea triennale funded only as a renewal of a prior 'Costruiamo il futuro' award. Both routes fund a full undergraduate degree over 3 academic years, so the degree_levels field is correctly 'Bachelor's'. The 'Costruiamo il futuro' scheme's own 2025-2026 terms (Article 7 of that Call) funded enrolment in Bachelor's Degree or single-cycle degree programmes from a reserve of twelve 9-month grants for final-year students at four Italian schools in Addis Ababa, Casablanca, Cairo and Tunis, with a maximum age of 23, and those holders are the population eligible for the 2026-2027 renewals recorded here.
